This public hearing is to consider an application from 102067804 Saskatchewan Limited for discretionary use approval to develop a car wash located on a site on the North West Corner of Pain Bend and Orban Way in the Evergreen neighborhood.
The site is undeveloped and is zoned before MX integrated commercial and mixed use district under the zoning by-law.
The purpose of this district is to facilitate mixed use development on the principal streets.
The district provides for a range of medium to high density residential uses commercial and institutional uses in a manner that encourages retail and service base uses at grade level.
And promotes a compact pedestrian oriented built form that supports transportation options, street oriented buildings and active uses at grade level.
A car wash is considered a discretionary use in this district.
The proposed car wash is to be constructed on the east side of the site where it will front on to Orban Way to meet the active furniture requirements of the district.
The building has been designed so the entry and exit to the car wash are internal to the site and it will have two commercial units that front onto Orban Way.
A hard surface audio space is also to be developed between the commercial units to accommodate a plaza or seating area.
This development will be part of a shopping center with other buildings to be built in the future on this site.
In October of this year, notice of this application was sent to property owners approximately 150 meters from the subject site.
The average evergreen community association in the word counselor notice of the application was also placed on the cities engage page.
No correspondence was received through the initial public engagement process.
However, following that public engagement a communication was received from the University of Saskatchewan noting that they didn't have any specific concerns with the proposed development.

This past week we did receive one other correspondence from a resident of the area noting some concerns with the car wash of this size and preferring to see other amenities that are more pedestrian oriented in the area.
Location of other approved discretionary uses are shown on appendix three of the report.
We have no concerns over the concentration or cumulative impacts of these discretionary uses.
This application does comply with the zoning by-lever requirements and it was reviewed by other civic departments who have advised they have no other concerns.

So to conclude public notice of this hearing has been provided in accordance with our established procedures and your administration is recommending that this discretionary use application be approved subject to the conditions outlined in our report.
